sentences.text:
1 Assailing the award dated 14/08/2018 passed by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Seonda, District Datia in Claim Case No. 57/2014 on the point of inadequacy of the compensation,
the appellants have preferred this appeal under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

entities.text:
Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Seonda, District Datia
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The accident in question took place on 29/7/2014 in which son of appellant no. 1 and brother of appellant No. 2 sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same during treatment on 1/8/2014.

Appellants/claimants had filed the claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 40,00,000/- on account of death of son of appellant No. 1 in an accident which took place on 29/7/2014.
However, Claims Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of application.

Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 29/7/2014 when deceased Sonu was travelling in a passenger bus bearing registration No. MP07F1263 towards his village Chaurai, as soon as bus reached near Cau Hotel, bus driver suddenly braked the bus due to which deceased fell down from bus and sustained grievous hurts and succumbed to the same during treatment on 1/8/2014.

According to appellants/claimants, the tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.5,000/- per month, whereas, the deceased was engaged in dairy work, agricultural activities etc and thereby used to earn Rs. 10,000/- per month and further the Claims Tribunal erred in deducting self dependency to the extent of 50% and further erred in applying the multiplier of 15 instead of 18 as per age of deceased to be 22 years at the accident and Claims Tribunal further erred in not awarding any amount under the head future prospects in light of decision of Apex Court in the matter o f National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors., 2017 ACJ 2700.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors., 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the same deserves to be enhanced.

The breakup of the amount of compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal is as under:-
Rs. 4,50,000/- towards loss of dependency Rs. 25,000/- towards funeral expenses Rs. 25,000/- towards loss of estate ------------------------------------------------------------------------ Rs. 5,00,000/- In total The respondent No. 3/Insurance Company has also filed cross- objections vide I.A.No. 1899/2019 under Order XLI Rule 22 of CPC assailing the impugned award on the ground of liability fastened over the Insurance Company as according to him on the date of incident, the deceased was under the influence of liquor and fell down from the bus and therefore, died and therefore,
Insurance Company cannot be fastened with the liability and thus, Claims Tribunal erred in holding that deceased died due to rash and negligence driver of the bus driver.

Further, at the most it is a case of contributory negligence of the deceased in causing the accident and therefore, learned Tribunal erred by not holding that incident in question was a result of the contributory negligence.

sentences.text: Counsel for respondent No. 1 and 2 argued in support of the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal as well as cross-objections.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

As regards the income of the deceased, in the opinion of this Court in absence of any documentary evidence regarding income of the deceased, the Claims Tribunal did not err in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs. 5,000/- per month.

As regards applying the multiplier of 15 as per the age of mother of deceased;
whereas, deceased was a major and already crossed the age of marriage of 21 years therefore, in the opinion of this Court, Claims Tribunal erred in applying the multiplier of 15 and instead it should be 18 as per the age of deceased at the time of accident.

As regard deduction of 50% towards self dependency, in the opinion of this Court,
since the deceased was unmarried and mother and brother were only dependent upon him, the Claim Tribunal did not err in deducting 50% towards self dependency.

Further in the opinion of this Court, the Claims Tribunal erred in not awarding any sum under the head future prospects and since the deceased was aged 22 years at the time of incident and was engaged in non-permanent job, claimants shall be entitled to receive 40% towards future prospects on behalf of deceased.

Thus by assessing the monthly income of the deceased to Rs. 5,000/- per month, his yearly income comes to Rs. 60,000/- and after deducting 50% towards self expenditure, the loss of yearly dependency comes to Rs. 30,000/-, and after adding 40% towards future prospects, the yearly loss comes to Rs. 30,000/- + 12,000/- =
42,000/- and after applying multiplier of 18 instead of 13 has been applied by Claims Tribunal total loss of dependency comes to Rs. 42,000 x 18 = 7,56,000/-.
The claimants shall also be entitled to receive Rs. 30,000/- towards loss of estate and funeral expenses in light of decision of Apex Court in the matter of Pranay Sethi (supra).
Thus, the total compensation comes to Rs. 7,56,000/- 30,000 =7,86,000/-.

The Claims Tribunal has already awarded a compensation of Rs. 5,00,000, therefore,
the claimants shall be entitled to receive an enhanced compensation of Rs. 7,86,000 - 5,00,000 = 2,86,000/-.

The enhanced amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.
2,86,000/- shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from July, 2017 when the decision of Apex Court in the matter of Pranay Sethi (supra) came into force and for rest of the amount the conditions as imposed of Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants/
claimants within four weeks' from today and proof thereof shall be submitted before the Registry.

Thereafter, Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed Smt. Mithlesh Kumar @ Mithleshi vs Mahendra Gupta on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8219947/

sentences.text:
A s regards, cross-objection filed on behalf of respondent No. 3/Insurance Company,
in the opinion of this Court, Insurance Company are misconceived and misplaced.

Even if it is assumed that deceased was intoxicated condition then also the evidence come on record cannot be falsified that due to sudden braking of bus by its driver,
deceased fell down and received grievous hurts and further contributory negligence can also not be fastened over the deceased as in the evidence of eye-witness Gulabsingh (PW/2) it has come that at the time of accident deceased was not in intoxicated condition.

Further postmortem report (Ex. P/7) and MLC report (Ex.
P/6) are also silent about this fact.

In the result, appeal filed by claimants is allowed in part to the extent indicated hereinabove and cross objections filed by respondent No. 3/Insurance Company vide I.A.No. 1899/2019 are hereby rejected.
Parties to bear their own cost.

(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
